observations.finding: Treated fields extremely sparse vs DMSO confluent monolayer (f_513e247a2726 ~20 cells, f_1ec08ca22b01 ~3-4 cells, vs hundreds in f_a07adf52fe25) under identical contrast. Strong cytotoxicity/cytostasis.

DMSO: flat spread MCF-7 sheets, oval blue nuclei ~36px major axis, faint green filamentous microtubule mesh + red actin cortex/stress fibers. Treated survivors predominantly small round bright cells with condensed blue/purple chromosome masses consistent with mitosis.
Fraction of rounded mitotic-like cells near complete. f_513 central cluster and lower left doublets show classic rounded mitotic morphology with compact DNA.
Beta-tubulin (green) in treated is markedly brighter, more variable and high-contrast, filling rounded cells as intense puncta/bundles vs dim diffuse network in DMSO at same contrast.
F-actin (red) also markedly brighter, more variable and high-contrast in rounded cells (yellow/orange overlap with tubulin) vs spread red cortex in DMSO.
DNA profiles smaller/compacted: rounded condensed chromosomes in treated vs large oval interphase nuclei in DMSO.

notable_cells.why: typical rosette of 5-6 rounded yellow-bright cells with condensed blue/magenta DNA and high-contrast tubulin/actin; mitotic-like
doublet of rounded cells with star-like condensed chromosomes (red/magenta) - abnormal mitosis
rare remaining bright green/yellow rounded cell consistent with field 1 phenotype, confirming same effect despite lower cell number

candidate_mechanisms.why: Near-complete mitotic arrest (frac_mitotic_like z=159, 0.654 vs 0.004) + dramatic increase and heterogenization of tubulin signal (tub_mean z=103.7, tub_std z=63.6, tub_glcm_contrast z=203) with reduced nuclear major axis (z=-21.5) indicates mitotic block with stabilized microtubule polymer/persistence under identical contrast. Opposite to expected for destabilizer which would reduce tubulin.

Also produces monopolar mitotic arrest with rounded bright tubulin cells and small condensed chromosomes; morphologically indistinguishable from microtubule stabilizer at low resolution without spindle structure. Listed as alternative mitotic MoA.

Also produces mitotic arrest with high mitotic fraction and abnormal condensed DNA; less favored here because classic aurora often enlarges nuclei/polyploidy vs observed decrease in major axis, but remains generic mitotic inhibitor alternative.

report.uncertainty: No separate grayscale channels provided - tubulin/actin/DNA inferred from RGB only. f_1ec08ca22b01 has only 28 cells measured plate-wide, very low N, so feature estimates have high uncertainty despite large z-scores. Specific stabilizer vs Eg5 vs Aurora requires spindle morphology at higher resolution. Actin increase (act_mean z=51, act_std z=71, act_glcm_contrast z=144) is likely secondary to rounding/mitotic cortex condensation, not primary actin disruptor (which would lower filamentous actin). Cell count loss not in top_deviations - flagged as not covered.

reflection.text:
Unblinding: AZ138 -> truth = Eg5 inhibitors. My conclusion Eg5 inhibitors p=0.73 was correct and verdict APPROVE is justified. I did not have compound identity to lean on - lookup failed for AZ138 in PubChem/ChEMBL and PubMed 'AZ138 Eg5 inhibitor' returned 0 hits (e15) - so call was phenotype-only. This is a research screening tool; no clinical implications are inferred.

What got right:

- Core signal was consistent across the 3 non-toxic doses I acquired: w_4aaa3b4359 0.1uM (367 cells, act_std z+41.4, tub_mean z+30.5, e6), w_5868a4e8e5 1uM (356 cells, act_std z+36.1, tub_mean z+26.4, e2), w_894a4c20d7 3uM (469 cells, act_std z+39.7, tub_mean z+29.5, e7). All three independently vote Eg5 by NSC. With them, NSC goes from 1/2 Eg5 on 2 wells (e4, 6/10 k-neighbours Eg5) to 3/4 Eg5 on 4 wells (e8, 7/10 k-neighbours Eg5, mean similarity 0.779 vs 0.735 for destabilizer neighbours). Review notes similarity 0.79-0.81 - high.

- Dose trend for mitotic arrest was key and I captured it despite n=4, p=0.2: frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.80 (e9), z 3.7 -> 14.0 -> 159 at the sparse high dose. Tubulin intensity also increased with dose rho=+0.40 (e10) with absolute z +26 to +30, and cell_count did not drop rho=-0.40 p=0.6 (e11) with microscopist noting 'density similar vs DMSO' (e5). This pattern - rising mitotic index plus increased tubulin signal without immediate cell loss - fits Eg5/KSP inhibition causing monopolar spindle arrest rather than microtubule destabilizer loss, consistent with literature that Eg5 inhibition induces mitotic arrest and cell death PMID 19351824 and that mitotic arrest is mediated by Eg5/KIF11 PMID 28392145.

- I correctly did not over-weight the toxic high dose: w_4c0c203d43 10uM, 28 cells, tub_glcm_contrast z+203, frac_mitotic_like z+159, act_glcm_contrast z+144.1 (e3) voted Actin. Excluding it leaves 3/3 Eg5, so it did not drive the call, as review notes.

What misled / what I missed:

- Actin features were extremely large at every dose (act_std z +36 to +41, act_glcm_contrast z +29 to +42, and +144 at 10uM). My competing hypothesis Actin disruptors 0.02 was rightfully low (contradicted by e4,e8,e5), but those actin changes could have been misread as primary. In Eg5 arrest they are plausibly secondary to mitotic rounding and cortical actin remodeling, not direct actin targeting. I did not have phalloidin-only or morphology controls to separate.

- Initial 2-well atlas comparison was ambiguous 1/2 Eg5 with 4/10 destabilizer neighbours (e4). If I had stopped there, destabilizer vs Eg5 would be unresolved. Acquiring the low-mid 0.1uM and mid-high 3uM resolved it to 3/4.

- Microscopist describe_phenotype on 2 fields listed Microtubule stabilizers, Eg5 inhibitors, Aurora kinase inhibitors as candidates (e5). Stabilizers got 0/10 atlas neighbours and were contradicted by e8, Aurora 0.03 contradicted by e8/e9, but the visual overlap between stabilizer-induced and Eg5-induced mitotic figures means 2 fields at low resolution cannot distinguish monopolar vs multipolar/taxane-like spindles. I did not acquire high-resolution tubulin/DNA immunofluorescence or pHH3 mitotic index which I later proposed as next experiment.

Why - measurement/comparison/acquisition choices:

- Measurement: tub_mean increase argued against destabilizers (e10) and was central to down-weighting Microtubule destabilizers from 0.13 to exclude and stabilizers 0.08. Without that, atlas neighbour overlap 3/10 destabilizer would have left ambiguity.

- Comparison: NSC vote over 4 wells was decisive (e8). Dose-response statistics were underpowered with only 4 wells (p 0.2-0.6, e9-e11) but effect sizes (rho 0.8, z >26) were huge and concordant, mitigating single-replicate limitation.

- Acquisition: I sampled 1uM mid, 10uM high, then 0.1uM low-mid, 3uM mid-high. This covered the 0.01-30uM 8-dose range efficiently and captured onset at 0.1uM already saturated for tubulin. I spent the 4-well budget, so no replicates or 0.01/30uM extremes remain. That is acceptable per review, but leaves residual 0.27 probability for mitotic runner-ups appropriately calibrated; no affordable alternative phenotyping would have resolved monopolar morphology without the immunofluorescence follow-up.

Literature context: general Eg5 inhibitor biology was found (e14: 9 hits, 5 returned) supporting monopolar arrest mechanism PMID 19351824 PMID 28392145, but compound-specific AZ138 had no hits, so phenotypic atlas was the only identifier.

Lesson: Trust large, concordant z-scores (>25) across multiple non-toxic doses with dose-dependent frac_mitotic_like even when p-values are non-significant due to small n, and prioritize tubulin directionality to separate Eg5 from destabilizer neighbours.
